items.what: .styluaignore is fully dead: its one entry, .claude/, names a hidden directory that StyLua never walks, so the file can be deleted
items.why: The gate and CI both run `stylua --check .` (StyLua 2.5.2). Tested outside the repository with the repository's stylua.toml and the same version: a badly formatted .claude/a.lua and .hid/a.lua are both skipped with no .styluaignore present, while vis/a.lua is reported; adding the ignore file changes nothing. StyLua's directory walk skips dot-prefixed paths, and a file passed by explicit path is not filtered by .styluaignore unless --respect-ignores is given, which nothing here passes. `rg --hidden styluaignore .` finds no reference in workflows, docs, AGENTS.md or the project profile. By contrast luacheck does walk hidden directories (tested the same way), so the '.claude/**' exclude in .luacheckrc is live. items.reason: For the repository's own invocations the claim holds: in a copy of the tree with StyLua 2.5.2, `stylua --check .` reports vis/a.lua and skips .claude/x.lua with or without .styluaignore, `stylua --check .claude/x.lua` reports it both ways, and CI, AGENTS.md, README and the profile all run plain `--check .` with no hook. But the file is not inert: `stylua --check --respect-ignores .claude/x.lua` passes with it and fails without it, and `stylua --check -a .` reports the two .claude files only without it, so deletion changes behaviour for an editor format-on-save integration (these commonly pass --respect-ignores) or any --allow-hidden run on worktree copies under .claude/; only the owner can say whether one is in use.

items.quote: - **Zone completion**: how much of a zone's Legacy objectives you've done, Guild Wars 2 style. Out of the box it counts areas explored (each is a step of the zone's Explore achievement, toward Explorer) for the character, and dungeons, raids and the zone's other Legacy objectives for your Legacy progress on the account. It can also show in the objective tracker, for the zone you're in (the zone name, a percentage and one row of counts), once you tick that in the map menu. Each can be collapsed, and hovering lists what's left. "What counts" in the same menu adds or leaves out any category, and the percentage and the toast follow.
